AffineDrift explains motion-capture *theory* in articles such as
[Motion Capture Technology](../articles/technology-motion-capture.html) and
[Markerless Motion Capture and Camera Selection](../articles/markerless-mocap-camera-selection.html).
This page records **what UpstreamDrift runs at one commit**, with links into the
implementing modules. Evidence URLs use
[`ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0)
(re-checked 2026-11-16 for issue #5623). The operator-facing step list mirrors
[`docs/motion_capture/user_guide.md`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/docs/motion_capture/user_guide.md);
the Capture Rig tile runs the same commands as
[`python3 -m motion_capture.rig`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/rig/__main__.py).

## Pipeline Overview {#pipeline-overview}

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Record / import video] --> B[Calibrate intrinsics]
  B --> C[Ingest 2-D poses]
  C --> D[Strobe sync offsets]
  D --> E[Bundle fit 3-D + cameras]
  E --> F[Temporal clean per joint]
  F --> G[Articulated model fit]
  G --> H[Export TRC / Simscape CSV]
```

Multi-camera sessions move through capture, lens calibration, per-view detection,
optional strobe-based time alignment, joint bundle adjustment, penalised temporal
smoothing, inverse-kinematics-style model fitting, and export. Single-camera
sessions can produce 2-D analysis or a prior-dependent image-space articulated
fit; they do not provide independently triangulated multi-view reconstruction.

### Stage Table (Commands and Artifacts)

| Stage | Primary module / CLI | Typical outputs under the session folder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Record | [`rig record`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/rig/__main__.py) | `plan.json`, `recordings.json`, `session_manifest.json`, per-view video |
| Intrinsics | [`rig calibrate-intrinsics`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/rig/__main__.py) | `intrinsics.json` (`K`, distortion, RMS) |
| Ingest | [`rig ingest`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/rig/__main__.py) | `observations/<view>.json` (or `observations_<estimator>/`) |
| Reconstruct | [`rig reconstruct --anchor SEG=M`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/rig/__main__.py) | `reconstruct/reconstruction.json`, `reconstruct/joints_3d_m.npy` |
| Model fit | Capture Rig / model stage | `model/joint_angles.json`, `model/fit_report.json`, `joint_angles_simscape.csv` |
| Export | [`reconstruct/export`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/export.py) | `reconstruct/reconstruction.trc`, `reconstruction_export.json` |

Synthetic regression bundles use
[`python3 -m motion_capture.reconstruct synth`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/__main__.py)
then
[`fit --anchor neck=…`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/__main__.py)
without the full rig UI.

## Real Video: Minimal Command Path


Expose the upstream packages in a Bash shell after installation:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD/src/shared/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
python3 -m src.motion_capture.rig import --out sessions/example --view front=front.mp4 --view side=side.mp4
python3 -m src.motion_capture.rig ingest --session sessions/example --estimator mediapipe
python3 -m src.motion_capture.rig reliability --session sessions/example
```

Before reconstruction, review the overlays, synchronization and weak joints.
Calibrate a **separate board session** at the same lens/resolution settings:

```bash
python3 -m src.motion_capture.rig calibrate-intrinsics --session sessions/board --board 9x6 --square 0.025
python3 -m src.motion_capture.rig reconstruct --session sessions/example --intrinsics sessions/board/intrinsics.json --anchor shank=0.42 --anchor forearm=0.26
python3 -m src.motion_capture.rig fit-model --session sessions/example
python3 -m src.motion_capture.rig export --session sessions/example
```

The lengths above are **example inputs**, not a default golfer. Measure the
subject. The first anchor fixes scale; additional measurements constrain the
other segments. For later takes with unchanged placement, replace `--intrinsics`
with `--cameras` pointing to the earlier `reconstruct/reconstruction.json`.
The [rig CLI](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/rig/__main__.py)
sets the per-view cleaning prior with `--accel-sigma-px`.

## Bundle Adjustment Problem {#bundle-adjustment}

The joint fitter is implemented in
[`bundle.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/bundle.py).
It solves one robust least-squares problem over all frames with residuals (in
physical units after division by $\sigma$):

$$
\begin{aligned}
r_{\text{repr}} &= \frac{w\,(\pi(\mathrm{cam}, X) - z)}{\sigma_{\mathrm{px}}} \\
r_{\text{bone}} &= \frac{|X_p - X_k| - L_k}{\sigma_{\mathrm{bone}}} \\
r_{\text{prior}} &= \frac{L_k - L_k^{\mathrm{prior}}}{\sigma_{\mathrm{prior}}} \\
r_{\text{sym}} &= \frac{L_{\mathrm{left}} - L_{\mathrm{right}}}{\sigma_{\mathrm{sym}}} \\
r_{\text{anchor}} &= \frac{L_{\mathrm{gauge}} - L_{\mathrm{measured}}}{\sigma_{\mathrm{anchor}}}
\end{aligned}
$$

Defaults are frozen in
[`BundleOptions`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/bundle.py):

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sigma_px` | 1.0 px | Reprojection weight scale |
| `sigma_bone_m` | 0.005 m (5 mm) | Segment rigidity |
| `sigma_prior_m` | 0.05 m (5 cm) | Anthropometric length prior |
| `sigma_symmetry_m` | 0.01 m (1 cm) | Left–right length pairing |
| `sigma_anchor_m` | 0.0002 m (0.2 mm) | Hard scale gauge from one tape measure |
| `sigma_measured_m` | 0.003 m (3 mm) | Additional tape-measured segments |
| `huber_delta` | 3.0 (in $\sigma_{\mathrm{px}}$ units) | Robust loss knee |
| `gate_px` | 6.0 px | Post-fit rejection and leave-one-out gate |

**Gauge freedom:** with one camera pose fixed, a global similarity about that
camera leaves every reprojection unchanged. The implementation therefore requires
a tape-measured anchor segment (`scale_anchor`) or accepts weak scale drift from
priors alone (documented in the `BundleOptions` docstring).

After convergence, observations whose reprojection exceeds `gate_px` are rejected;
a leave-one-out test can blame additional points
([`_leave_one_out_rejections`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/bundle.py)).

### Weighted DLT Initialization

Per-frame triangulation before bundle iteration uses weighted DLT rows
$\sqrt{w}\,(u p_3 - p_1)$ and $\sqrt{w}\,(v p_3 - p_2)$ in
[`geometry.dlt`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/geometry.py).
First-order point covariance is
$\Sigma_X = \sigma_{\mathrm{px}}^2 (J^\top J)^+$ with $J = \partial(u,v)/\partial X$
per view
([`_covariance`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/geometry.py)).
That matches the multiview formula on the camera-selection article when
$\Sigma_u = \sigma^2 I$, but **does not** fold calibration or timing uncertainty
into $\Sigma_X$.

The standalone triangulation and bundle gates are different defaults:

| Quantity | Default at the Pin |
|---|---|
| Triangulation gate | 8 px |
| Bundle rejection gate | 6 px |

Two useful views suffice for a geometric solution, but not generally for
leave-one-out blame assignment; a third useful view supplies redundancy.

### Strobe Timing (Not Exposure Midpoint)

Cross-camera alignment uses arrival timestamps plus strobe-derived offsets in
[`rig/sync.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/rig/sync.py).
Uncertainty is on the order of one frame interval per camera (combined in
quadrature between pairs), which differs from exposure-midpoint timing models
discussed generically in the camera-selection article.

### Synthetic Harness Acceptance

UpstreamDrift’s unit test
[`test_synth_then_fit_writes_reconstruction_with_metrics`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/tests/motion_capture/reconstruct/test_fit_cli.py)
runs `synth` (24 frames) then `fit` with a neck anchor from `truth.json` and
asserts, among other checks: `rms_px < 2.0`, per-camera `rotation_deg < 0.5`,
and max relative bone-length error `< 5 %`. These are **CI thresholds on a
synthetic lab rig**, not field guarantees.

Example commands (from repository root, `PYTHONPATH` set as in UpstreamDrift):

```bash
python3 -m src.motion_capture.reconstruct synth --out sessions/synthetic-example --frames 120
python3 -m src.motion_capture.reconstruct fit --bundle sessions/synthetic-example --anchor neck=0.53
```

## Temporal Smoothing {#temporal-smoothing}

Reconstruction applies
[`temporal.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/temporal.py)
per scalar channel. The objective penalises measurement error (Huber-weighted) plus
a discrete acceleration prior:

$$
\min \sum_t \frac{c_t}{\sigma_z^2}\,\rho(x_t - z_t)
  + \sum_t \left(\frac{x_{t-1} - 2 x_t + x_{t+1}}{\Delta t^2}\right)^2 \frac{1}{\sigma_a^2}
$$

`acceleration_sigma` is in **physical units per second squared** (pixels/s² before
3-D, metres/s² or radians/s² after model fit). `SmootherOptions` defaults include
`huber_delta = 2.5`, `gate_sigma = 5.0`, and `detection_tightening = 10.0` for
outlier detection
([`SmootherOptions`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/temporal.py)).

Rig cleaning uses `--accel-sigma-px`, default **20,000 px/s²**. The separate
`fit-model` parser defaults to 300 rad/s² for its angular acceleration prior
and 25 rad/s for speed reporting. The [model CLI parser](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/rig/_cli_parsers.py)
names those controls. Rejected observations and bound violations remain in the
reports; a small residual alone does not certify physical acceptance.

The legacy motion-pipeline path still exposes a **Butterworth low-pass** with
`cutoff = 6.0` Hz and `order = 2` by default in
[`motion_pipeline/preprocessing/filter.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/motion_pipeline/preprocessing/filter.py).
That default is appropriate to gait-scale motion; golf downswing peaks require
the reconstruction smoother or an explicit cutoff choice, not the silent 6 Hz
default.

## Anthropometric Scaling in Code {#anthropometric-scaling}

[Chapter 23 of *The Physics of Golf*](../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/ch23_dof_urdf_models.html#anthropometric-data-de-leva-1996)
states de Leva segment definitions correctly. UpstreamDrift applies those tables
in two different places:

### Ratio Estimators (`anthropometrics`)

[`_segment_properties_from_ratios`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/anthropometrics/estimators/_base.py)
builds each segment with

- $m = (\text{mass ratio})\,M$,
- $L = (\text{length ratio})\,H$,
- COM at $(0, 0, c L)$ along segment **$z$** from the proximal landmark,
- $I = \mathrm{diag}\bigl(m(k_{\mathrm{sag}} L)^2, m(k_{\mathrm{trans}} L)^2, m(k_{\mathrm{long}} L)^2\bigr)$.

[`DeLevaEstimator`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/anthropometrics/estimators/from_de_leva.py)
reads the shared builder `DE_LEVA_DATA` table, including its model length ratios.
Its name therefore does not guarantee published de Leva endpoint lengths. **`DempsterEstimator` and
`ZatsiorskyEstimator` use different ratio tables** and must not be swapped in
without checking segment definitions.

### Humanoid Character Builder

The 22-segment golfer template in
[`humanoid_character_builder/core/anthropometry.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/humanoid_character_builder/core/anthropometry.py)
applies **de Leva mass, COM, and gyration radii to builder length ratios**
(`_GEOMETRY`), not necessarily de Leva’s published segment lengths. Example:
male `upper_arm` length ratio `0.186` of stature versus de Leva’s
$0.2817/1.741 \approx 0.162$ when stature is normalised to de Leva’s reference.
Inertia therefore scales roughly as $(L_{\mathrm{model}}/L_{\mathrm{de\,Leva}})^2$
relative to a literal de Leva length assignment. Virtual neck, shoulder, and hip
links carve mass from parents with placeholder radii (`VIRTUAL_SEGMENTS`).

Both paths use **de Leva radii with builder lengths**. The ratio estimator uses
**longitudinal $z$**. The separate [cylinder inertia estimator](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/anthropometrics/estimators/from_inertia_calc.py)
uses **longitudinal $x$**; rotate tensors into the same frame before comparing.

For a male upper arm, builder length is $0.186H$, while the cited de Leva
endpoint length is $0.2817/1.741$ of stature. At fixed mass and radius fraction,

$$
\frac{I_{builder}}{I_{publication\ length}}
=\left(\frac{0.186}{0.2817/1.741}\right)^2\approx1.321.
$$

For $H=1.741$ m the two lengths are 0.323826 m and 0.2817 m: about 32% more
inertia from length alone. Mass carve-outs and frame differences are additional
effects. This is a worked sensitivity calculation, not a subject validation.
[The anthropometry chapter](../articles/The_Physics_of_Golf/quarto/ch23_dof_urdf_models.html)
provides the broader modelling context.



## Bring Your Own Data {#bring-your-own-data}

Reference fitting and C3D import are documented in
[`docs/motion_capture/reference_model_fitting.md`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/docs/motion_capture/reference_model_fitting.md)
and implemented in
[`reference/fitting.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reference/fitting.py).

| Input | Mechanism | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Multi-view video | `rig import` / `record` | Same bundle layout as live capture |
| C3D / marker labs | Profile JSON (`name`, `units`, `axes`, `joints`) | Centroid of listed markers; NaN rows are **not** interpolated |
| Tour-average proxies | Bundled profile | Waist ≈ hips, `BackTop` ≈ neck—approximations, not joint centres |
| FreeMoCap / OpenCap | Ingest sidecars | Marker sets mapped toward reconstruction names |
| CSV / JSON motion | Capture export conventions | See `capture_export.to_capture_frame` |
| BVH / TRC / MOT / native SMPL | — | **No reader in this slice** at the pin; HMR2/SMPL may appear only as sidecars |

`axes` example for Tour Average: `["+X", "-Z", "+Y"]` converts source Y-up data to
right-handed Z-up metres before fitting.

### Complete C3D Profile Example

The [reference fitting job](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/docs/motion_capture/reference_model_fitting.md)
accepts a saved JSON job and a C3D marker profile. Start from the upstream example:

```bash
python3 -m src.motion_capture.reference.fit_job --list-models
python3 -m src.motion_capture.reference.fit_job --config examples/motion_capture/reference_driver.json
```

Change `source`, `profile` and the output directory for another capture. Keep its
actual clock; a stride selects samples without relabelling the source timestamps.
The following complete **synthetic label mapping** illustrates the profile shape;
replace every marker label with one in your own file:

```json
{
  "name": "example_y_up_markers",
  "units": "mm",
  "axes": ["+X", "-Z", "+Y"],
  "joints": {
    "mid_hip": ["LWaist", "RWaist"],
    "neck": ["BackTop"],
    "nose": ["Nose"],
    "left_shoulder": ["LShoulder"],
    "left_elbow": ["LElbow"],
    "left_wrist": ["LWrist"],
    "right_shoulder": ["RShoulder"],
    "right_elbow": ["RElbow"],
    "right_wrist": ["RWrist"],
    "left_hip": ["LHip"],
    "left_knee": ["LKnee"],
    "left_ankle": ["LAnkle"],
    "right_hip": ["RHip"],
    "right_knee": ["RKnee"],
    "right_ankle": ["RAnkle"]
  }
}
```

`axes` gives the signed source axes assigned to canonical X, Y, Z. This map
converts Y-up to right-handed Z-up; an odd permutation without the compensating
sign would reflect the body. Canonical reference motion is in Z-up metres;
registration then maps it into the fitter/camera **Y-up** world. Name that
boundary before comparing with the [site frame](notation.html#coordinate-frame-conventions).
Multiple marker labels mean their centroid, requiring every constituent to be
valid. Unknown labels fail explicitly. Missing samples remain **NaN** and are
**not interpolated** through during fitting. Waist and BackTop markers are
surface proxies for hips and neck, not anatomical joint centres.

Video import is the rig route above. FreeMoCap and OpenCap have separate
adapters/sidecar workflows; their existence does not mean every reference job
accepts arbitrary exports. Use the [upstream adapter inventory](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/docs/motion_capture/self_calibrating_pipeline.md)
for the specific route and format. A TRC marker input in the downstream motion
pipeline is distinct from C3D reference fitting. A monocular SMPL sidecar is
also distinct from triangulated marker evidence.

## Generated Models and Conversion {#generated-models}

Model templates and URDF/MJCF writers live under
[`src/shared/python/model_generation`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/model_generation)
and
[`src/tools/model_converter`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/tools/model_converter).
Composite joints (gimbal, universal) expand into intermediate links named
`<joint>_intermediate_k` / `<joint>_dofk` with mass
[`INTERMEDIATE_LINK_MASS = 0.001` kg](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/model_generation/core/constants.py)
as numerical mass regularization, not a remedy for a kinematic singularity. Segment axes, limits, and
the 22-segment layout are enumerated in
[`segment_definitions.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/humanoid_character_builder/core/segment_definitions.py).
`golfer_canonical.yaml` drives converter output; default MJCF integrator settings
include `timestep 0.002` with RK4 where the template specifies it.

Articulated fit after reconstruction uses
[`reconstruct/model/fit.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/model/fit.py)
and [`fit2d.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/motion_capture/reconstruct/model/fit2d.py)
for image-space matching on single-view paths.

### Commands and Joint Expansion

The [canonical converter](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/tools/model_converter/build_models.py)
validates `golfer_canonical.yaml` and exports URDF, MJCF and Simscape parameter
files. It is a separate model-construction path from fitting a capture:

```bash
python3 -m src.tools.model_converter --validate-only
python3 -m src.tools.model_converter --urdf-out generated-example/golfer.urdf --drake-urdf-out generated-example/drake.urdf --mjcf-out generated-example/golfer.xml --matlab-out generated-example/InitModelParameters.m
```

Specify every output to keep generated experiments outside canonical model files.
This command does not promise an OpenSim `.osim` export or invert an arbitrary
engine model. Read joint names, axis order and limits from the chosen template;
DOF counts and native joint semantics differ between models.

The separate [composite-joint expander](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/model_generation/core/composite_joints.py)
turns a default gimbal into Z→Y→X revolutes (`<joint>_dof1` to `dof3`), with
`<joint>_intermediate_1` and `_2`; a universal joint uses X→Y with one
`<joint>_intermediate` link. Custom composite axes override those defaults.
The intermediate links carry **0.001 kg** and diagonal inertia **1e-6 kg·m²**;
"near-massless" is a numerical regularization, not zero physical inertia.
Do not apply this expander's conventions automatically to the canonical
converter or a native OpenSim custom joint.

## MyoFullBody Static Optimisation (As Implemented) {#myofullbody}

Hybrid static optimisation for muscle-driven residuals is in
[`myofullbody/redundancy.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/myofullbody/redundancy.py).
Each frame solves

$$
\min \sum a^2 + w \sum \mathrm{reserve}^2
\quad\text{s.t.}\quad
\tau = R^\top (F_{\mathrm{passive}} + a \odot F_{\mathrm{active}}) + \mathrm{reserve},
$$

with $R = (-\mathrm{actuator\_moment})\,\Phi$ and $\Phi$ the rate map from
[`mapping.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/tree/ca9d8887f2ed46de484b64615dd4a50148e07bd0/src/shared/python/myofullbody).
Reserve actuators cover every spec coordinate; their RMS measures what muscles
cannot reproduce.
